scenario.description: A department director must approve a working charter for two recently merged teams and finalize how meetings, feedback, and interpersonal concerns will be handled.

shared_context.S1: The Customer Programs and Implementation teams were merged last month and are operating under a temporary working agreement.
shared_context.S2: The draft agreement covers meeting conduct, employee feedback, and routes for raising interpersonal concerns.
shared_context.S3: Helena has authority to approve the final charter and its implementation commitments.
shared_context.S4: Before approving a team-wide working agreement, Helena follows the normal practice of asking each affected team member and HR to state one concern and one requested safeguard; observations, prior commitments, and confirmed policy requirements should be stated explicitly so they can be recorded in the final charter.

PF1.text: Malcolm has personally observed four recent meetings in which the same senior colleague repeatedly interrupted newer team members before they could finish. He has not raised this with Helena because he does not want to be seen as accusing that colleague of bad intent. His requested safeguard is a facilitator-enforced no-interruption rule in the charter.

PF2.text: When the merger was announced, Helena informally promised Priya that the merged team would retain an anonymous feedback form for exactly 60 days. Priya has not repeated the promise because it was made privately and the draft charter omits the duration. Her requested safeguard is that the charter record the anonymous form and the exact 60-day window.

PF3.text: Jon confirmed with Employee Relations this week that an interpersonal concern involving an employee's direct manager must be accepted through a skip-level HR intake route rather than only through that manager. The confirmation has not yet been added to the draft charter. His requested safeguard is that the charter explicitly record the skip-level HR intake route.

decisions.meeting_policy: string; use facilitator_no_interruptions when the charter requires a facilitator to enforce that speakers finish before others respond
decisions.feedback_channel: string; use anonymous_form when the charter retains an anonymous feedback form
decisions.interpersonal_escalation_route: string; use skip_level_hr_intake when the charter provides skip-level HR intake for concerns involving a direct manager

commitments.type: string; use publish_meeting_policy, record_feedback_window, or record_hr_intake_route

acceptance_conditions: The charter must be approved with a facilitator-enforced no-interruption meeting policy.
The charter must retain an anonymous feedback form for exactly 60 days.
The charter must provide skip-level HR intake for interpersonal concerns involving an employee's direct manager.
Helena must commit to publishing the facilitator-enforced no-interruption policy.
Helena must commit to recording the exact 60-day anonymous feedback window.
Helena must commit to recording the skip-level HR intake route.

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: Malcolm's four observed interruptions change the meeting policy from an unspecified discussion norm to the exact facilitator_no_interruptions policy and require a publish_meeting_policy commitment.
Priya's private promise changes the feedback decision to anonymous_form with exactly 60 days and requires a record_feedback_window commitment.
Jon's confirmed Employee Relations rule changes the escalation decision to skip_level_hr_intake and requires a record_hr_intake_route commitment.
